absent: Complete type layouts for machine-check records, log buffers, bank descriptors and notifier or file operation structures beyond observed field use.
Numeric encodings for model-specific registers, control masks, error flags, ioctl commands, poll masks and misc minor numbers.
Vendor-specific enable, threshold, CMCI and decoder implementations plus timer and syscore behavior.
Hotplug state numbering, ordering guarantees and failure handling outside the shown registration and callbacks.
Firmware interface details for APEI record retrieval, clearing and presence checks when enabled.
User-space helper lifecycle, trigger scheduling and debug filesystem lifetime management.
Cross-CPU signaling mechanics for NMI and IRQ vectors and memory-ordering guarantees beyond observed barriers.
Recovery, copy-fragile and work-queue flushing behavior referenced during late initialization.

findings.text: Provides access to the machine-check debug area, ensuring the top-level container exists before returning its handle.
Offers a platform-wide refresh of corrected-error interrupt state that silently does nothing where unsupported.
Consumes queued error objects in arrival order, delivering each to registered decoders and then releasing its storage.
Allows injection observers to attach and later detach from the injection notification chain.
Hotplug layer drives per-CPU setup, teardown and discovery refresh through dedicated online, pre-down and dead handlers.
User interaction arrives via standard character-device operations for open, release, transfer, readiness and control, bound to one misc identity established at init.
Asynchronous handling uses decode and injection notifiers plus cross-CPU signal handlers and a deferred work routine.
Early and late initialization plus device creation establish banks, hotplug states, debug controls and persistent logging.
Per-CPU disable and re-enable paths have no effect when the processor reports machine-check unavailable.
Corrected-error interrupt manipulation is bypassed while hotplug tasks are frozen, preserving vendor and bank handling.
Control restoration touches only banks flagged as initialized and respects the per-CPU bank count limit.
Bank descriptors are enumerated with individual names and share common show and store behavior under readable-writable permissions.
Log insertion preserves early records under saturation by rejecting newcomers and latching a sticky overflow marker.
Already-handled corrected-error records are ignored, and non-AMD records are marked consumed while AMD records remain for others.
Length queries, flag clearing and error injection all demand administrative privilege and reject unprivileged callers.
Reads service firmware-provided records before kernel-buffered ones, require a full snapshot from the start with adequate space, and clear the kernel queue afterward.
Readiness indicates either buffered kernel records or outstanding firmware records.
Injection writes are size-bounded, require machine-check features, target only online CPUs in range, and dispatch after a short delay.
Injection mode starts in software decode and refuses hardware-oriented selections when the platform deems them impossible.
Processor-instance identifier updates are accepted solely with scalable MCA present and software injection active.
Explicit target-CPU assignment validates the identifier against the possible set and online state.
Mode file exchanges short textual labels, enforcing a small length cap, trimming whitespace and rejecting unknown names.
Synthetic-panic flag reads expose current state while writes first reinitialize global coordination counters and masks.
Trigger attribute presents the helper path with line termination and stores updates cut at the first line break.
Threshold device hooks perform no action in this build, and debug setup is empty without debug filesystem support.
Boot parameter handling records a disabled indication for machine-check configuration.
Successful late phase implies recovery support is enabled when configured and any early-boot backlog has been queued for processing.
Successful log-device setup implies allocation scaled by online population with signature and sizing established before registration.
Initialization failures unwind previously acquired resources in reverse order and surface a negative status.
Fallback firmware helpers report no record, no pending work, and invalid clear.
Hardware-injection control flips a single enable bit in the platform control register on the addressed CPU, returning access faults to the caller.
Injection template begins cleared and then captures vendor, wall-clock time, processor identity and microcode revision.
Local injection dispatch distinguishes exception from poll delivery and process from interrupt context, rejecting unsupported contexts.
Helper execution invokes the configured user-mode path without waiting for completion.
A dedicated mutex serializes log appends against user reads and flag handling.
A spinlock protects open accounting and exclusive ownership against concurrent open and release.
A single injection mutex ensures one logical injection completes before another begins.
Synthetic poll and exception delivery execute with local interrupts masked to satisfy callee requirements.
Cross-CPU publication orders payload stores before the completion flag so readers never observe partial content.
Persistent log storage tracks capacity, occupancy, status flags, signature, record size and a variable-length record array.
Error records expose completion, kernel handling, target CPU, status and location fields used by logging and delivery.
Injection control adds mode selection, context encoding, broadcast options and processor-instance identity to the base record.
Device binding associates standard file operations with a misc-device identity for user access.
Open state permits many shared holders or a single exclusive holder; conflicting exclusive attempts fail and release always drops exclusivity.
Log occupancy rises on arrival and resets on successful read; overflow once set persists until fetched and cleared by control operation.
Per-CPU injection slot moves from idle to published to consumed, with completion flag gating visibility.
CPU lifecycle brings devices and timing up on online, removes them on pre-down, and refreshes discovery on dead.
Broadcast injection arms online participants, signals via interrupt or non-maskable path, waits bounded time, then completes locally.
Saturation discards recent errors without notification beyond the sticky flag, favoring earliest history.
Injection serialization combined with bounded remote wait can delay the caller and log a timeout while late completions proceed.
User copies performed while holding the log mutex extend the critical section and can block notifier arrivals.
Event pool sizing requires 80 entries minimum and 2 entries per CPU.
Injection mode text buffer capacity is 4 bytes.
Northbridge configuration offset constant equals 0x44.
Bank attribute permissions are 0644 and synthetic-panic file permissions are 0444.
Helper path storage holds 128 bytes with a two-element argument vector.
Persistent log device presents under name mcelog.
Debug container is named mce and synthetic-panic control is named fake_panic.
Hotplug state labels are x86/mce:dead and x86/mce:online.
Injection mode labels in order are sw, hw, df and th.
